item.title: true or false in CSS
item.content:encoded: CSS doesn’t have a boolean type, but it does have the true and false keywords. Register a custom property that only accepts them, flip it with :has(), and container style queries turn messy :checked selector combinations into readable conditions.

item.title: Data Access Testing With @testcontainers
item.content:encoded: Testing data access code has always been awkward: unit tests want to be fast and isolated, and a real database is neither. With Docker and @testcontainers you can spin up a throwaway Postgres inside your Vitest suite, push your Drizzle schema into it, and verify that your real insert and query code round-trips correctly.

item.title: Multi-Column Different-Speed Scrolling
item.content:encoded: Scroll-Driven Animations can step in and make scrolling feel different even if you aren't actually interfering with the actual page scroll.

item.title: Overriding Heading Levels With the headingoffset HTML Attribute
item.content:encoded: The new headingoffset HTML attribute lets you bump a heading’s level up by adding to it, which is handy when a component’s h1 needs to be an h2 somewhere else. Here’s how the math works, how to reset it, how to style the result with :heading(), and where aria-level fits in.

item.title: Two Circles, One Connection, and border-shape
item.content:encoded: Swapping the clip-path arrow from the previous article for border-shape and shape(), we can connect two draggable circles with fancy curved lines that stay perfectly aligned.

item.title: Useful @custom-media Presets
item.content:encoded: Custom media queries let you name and reuse media queries the way custom properties do for values. Here’s a set of drop-in @custom-media presets for input mechanisms, breakpoints, and true HDR, plus a container style query version of each that works in every browser today.

item.title: How I Used Claude Code to Speed Up My Shell Startup by 95%
item.content:encoded: I like the idea of "Please suggest 10 improvements to my ~/.zshrc" as a prompt (John Lindquist). Nick Taylor wrote up all the stuff it found for him and got nearly a second back for every fresh terminal opened.

item.title: Building an Isolated Preview for AI-Generated HTML
item.content:encoded: An iframe with srcdoc feels like a safe place to render HTML a model wrote. It isn't. Three tests show how the preview can read your page, escape the frame, and phone home, and four layers of protection close each hole.
